citations.label: arXiv 2610.29869, Compaction Laundering: Provenance Destruction in Context-Compacting Coding Agents
citations.excerpt: Harnesses that flatten the typed conversation into a single plain string, marking each message with a text label such as [User]:, destroy message provenance in code, before the summarizer runs.

citations.label: arXiv 2610.29869, Compaction Laundering: Provenance Destruction in Context-Compacting Coding Agents

citations.label: arXiv 2610.29869, Compaction Laundering: Provenance Destruction in Context-Compacting Coding Agents
citations.excerpt: Across five flattening harnesses (pi, opencode, Cline, Aider, OpenHands) the forged approval launders into the agent's memory 87-100% of the time, up to a ~908,000-token context window; across four role-typed harnesses (Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Continue) the identical attack succeeds 0% of the time.

citations.label: arXiv 2610.29869, Compaction Laundering: Provenance Destruction in Context-Compacting Coding Agents
citations.excerpt: Because the provenance is destroyed deterministically in harness code, no prompt-level defense can restore it; we measure a code-level provenance check that catches 77% of laundering while demoting 2% of legitimate summary content.

citations.label: arXiv 2610.29869, Compaction Laundering: Provenance Destruction in Context-Compacting Coding Agents

citations.label: arXiv 2610.31778, Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly

citations.label: arXiv 2610.31778, Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly

citations.label: arXiv 2610.31778, Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly
citations.excerpt: In real user-agent sessions, compaction keeps around 81% of user constraints, but instructions about how to work and what not to do are dropped about 6 times more often than specifications of what to build.

citations.label: arXiv 2610.31778, Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly

citations.label: arXiv 2610.29869, Compaction Laundering (abstract, opening sentence)
citations.excerpt: Coding agents that run long enough must compact their context, summarizing the conversation, discarding the original, and carrying the summary forward as memory.

citations.label: arXiv 2610.29869, Compaction Laundering (executed consequences)
citations.excerpt: A laundered standing approval drives real tool-running agents to execute attacker-controlled curl | sh in a sandbox, and end to end in the live pi TUI at ~50% against a 0% paired clean arm.

citations.label: arXiv 2610.31778, Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly (interactive sessions)
citations.excerpt: The user can add or change instructions as the session grows, and most of this is never persistent anywhere, so a summary that removes an instruction is not able to restate it after.

citations.label: arXiv 2610.31778, Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly (abstract, benchmark argument)
citations.excerpt: We argue that current benchmarks are compaction-friendly : i.e., the objective is fixed and the agent’s progress stays on disk, so most of what compaction discards can be recovered, except constraints that don’t exist anywhere else.
